reason: The code path and cited lines hold, but the record's description, blockers and validation plan are out of date after the parent's l9 checks. (1) The claim that the pressure is self-releasing at exec_timeout (timeout's group kill, exit 124) is refuted live. In l9_agent_pressure.out line 7 the agent exec returned exit 254 after 34 s, from bash 'fork: retry' failures, so timeout never fired. About 1000 uid-1000 'tail' processes survived. pids stayed at 1022/1024 after the exec returned (l9 line 8) and after the parent's own pkill (line 9). l9_probe.out line 2 shows 1002 tails in state S. The mock in v09_policy.out line 3 does not carry over. (2) Blocker 1 is mostly answered. Agent-only exec pressure through box.call_tool (policy allow) drove the cgroup to 1024/1024 (l9 line 4). The next agent GUI input returned 200 and recorded a burst whose baseline manifest had 0 entries; the audit showed only tool_request, policy_decision, snapshot and tool_result (l9 lines 5-6). (3) What is still not shown is the end-to-end gui_changes outcome on the agent-only path. Because the pressure never released, the close step in l9 produced no gui_changes record (line 10). The close-time manifest was also empty, and the 'real change' written by docker exec under a full pid cgroup probably did not run. That is not evidence of evasion, so the record stays needs_validation and is not promoted. The record also leaves out that kill_processes and desktop_processes are likewise starved. I re-read the cited lines in the audited tree and they are correct: service.py 210/221/238/246/264/341, sandbox.py 495-501/686-697, api.py 205-206, default_policy.yaml read-only-exec, and the cited lines of the l7 and v09 outputs. The fingerprint is unchanged and the corrected record keeps the same root cause.

record.title: GUI burst open treats failed container-side collection as success (empty baseline or no burst) with no audit record
record.description: When the first agent GUI input of a burst arrives, AgentBox._snapshot takes a docker-commit snapshot and then calls _open_gui_burst. That method collects the /workspace manifest and the desktop process baseline. Two silent fail-open paths exist. (a) Exit status unchecked (observed live): SandboxManager.workspace_manifest runs the root `find ... | head -c` exec and returns `_parse_manifest(res.output[0] or b"")` without checking res.exit_code. If the in-container command cannot run, it returns ({}, False) with no exception, and _open_gui_burst records the burst against an empty baseline. desktop_processes and kill_processes ignore exec status in the same way. At close, the diff would report every pre-existing file as added. The audit event carries counts and truncated=True plus only the first 100 sorted paths, so the real GUI-made change can fall outside the listed paths, and nothing records that the baseline collection failed. Parent-live l7 measured this on agentbox-desktop:0.1 with the pids cgroup at 1022-1024/1024, using pressure created by direct docker exec as uid 1001: the manifest had 0 entries, the burst was recorded, the audit showed only tool_request/policy_decision/snapshot/tool_result, and a close after the pressure ended gave gui_changes added=301, truncated=True, with the real change zz_changed_by_gui.txt absent from the listed 100. (b) Exception swallowed: if either collector raises, the bare `except Exception: return` at service.py:210 records no burst. Later GUI inputs inside the idle/interval window open no new burst, so there is no stray kill and no gui_changes for that window. The same pattern at :221 and :238 skips the kill or the diff at close. A mock reproduces this, but no agent-reachable raising trigger is known: it needs a Docker API error such as the container gone or not running, or the docker client's 60 s read timeout. Pid pressure reaches path (a), not :210. Agent reachability (parent-live l9, after Phase 3): the default policy allows an approval-free exec of `tail -f /dev/null & ` x1100 + `tail -f /dev/null` (rule read-only-exec, uid 1000, which the stray killer never targets). Through box.call_tool as the agent this took the pids cgroup to 1024/1024 within about 1 s. A concurrent agent GUI input (key shift) still returned 200 and recorded a burst with 0 manifest entries and no audit marker. Correction to the earlier description: the pressure does not release itself. When pids run out, the exec ends early with exit 254 (bash fork retries fail), so exec_timeout never fires. The ~1000 uid-1000 tails survived, pids stayed at 1022/1024 after the exec returned and after a root `pkill -x tail` by the parent, and a close under that pressure logged no gui_changes at all (the close-time manifest was empty too). A sandbox wedged this way can run no new processes, which limits what the agent can do while the condition holds. Not yet shown: an agent-only sequence that ends with a gui_changes record that is misleading (added=301, truncated, real change unlisted) or absent despite a real GUI-made change, which needs the pressure released, or a GUI change that needs no new process (for example a shell builtin in a terminal opened earlier). Bounds: the burst snapshot is still taken and logged, so the restore point survives. In the measured cases ps still ran, so the stray-kill baseline was populated. gui_changes is a detective, partial control: the GUI is approval-free by design (N-1).
record.claimed_root_cause: Burst bookkeeping treats a failed container-side collection as a successful one. workspace_manifest (sandbox.py:499-501), desktop_processes (sandbox.py:689-692) and kill_processes (sandbox.py:697) never check exec exit status, and _open_gui_burst/_stop_gui_strays/_close_gui_burst (service.py:210, 221, 238) swallow every exception. In both cases there is no audit event and no fail-closed fallback, such as refusing further GUI input or marking the burst baseline invalid.

trace.description: Agent token (lowest-trust principal, own sandbox) sends a GUI input tool (key/click/type). Policy default is allow, with no approval.
On an allowed GUI input that starts a burst (_gui_needs_snapshot true), it calls _snapshot.
After docker commit, it opens the GUI burst with the new snapshot id.
Root find exec result is parsed without checking exit_code. A failed exec (e.g. no free pid in the cgroup) returns ({}, False) instead of raising.

Burst is recorded with the empty manifest as its baseline, with no audit event marking the collection as failed. A later gui_changes diff against a healthy manifest would report all existing files as added and can leave the real change out of the 100 listed paths.

evidence.description: except Exception: return in _open_gui_burst. A raising collector leaves no burst and no audit record.
except Exception: return in _stop_gui_strays. A failed ps/xdotool/kill skips the stray kill silently.
except Exception: return in _close_gui_burst. A failed close-time manifest skips gui_changes silently.
gui_changes lists only v[:100] of each sorted diff list plus counts and a truncated flag, so an empty baseline buries the real change.
desktop_processes ignores the ps exit status. A failed exec yields an empty process list.
kill_processes ignores the kill exec's exit status.
read-only-exec allow rule includes tail. simple_programs treats & as a separator, so a ~1000-way background `tail -f /dev/null` exec is approval-free.
Live: under pid pressure (uid 1001 sleepers by direct docker exec), workspace_manifest returned 0 entries with no exception.
Live: first GUI input still 200, burst recorded with baseline manifest entries 0.
Live: after pressure ends, the next GUI input opens no new burst (needs_snapshot False), so the degraded burst persists.
Live: close gives gui_changes added=301, truncated=True, and the real change is not in the listed 100 paths. Control at line 3 shows added=1 with the change listed.
Live (after Phase 3): the agent's approval-free exec (policy allow) drove pids to 1024/1024 within about 1 s, before the GUI input.
Live: the agent's GUI input under that pressure returned 200 and recorded a burst with 0 manifest entries.
Live: the audit shows only tool_request, policy_decision, snapshot and tool_result, with no event marking the failed collection.
Live: the agent exec ended with exit 254 after 34 s while pids stayed at 1022/1024. exec_timeout never fired, so the pressure is not self-releasing (this contradicts the earlier mock).
Live: with the pressure persisting, the close logged no gui_changes record. The close-time manifest was empty as well, so the end-to-end misleading-diff result via the agent-only path is not shown.
Live: after the exec returned, about 1002 uid-1000 tail processes remained in state S, so they were not killed.
Mock: a raising workspace_manifest at open leaves no burst. Lines 3-5 show only the snapshot event, no new burst on the next input, no kill, no gui_changes.

Real SandboxManager collectors with a fake container whose exec exits 126: workspace_manifest returns ({}, False), desktop_processes returns ([], set()), and kill_processes returns, all without raising.
Real _close_gui_burst with an empty baseline: counts added=301, truncated=True, real change not listed. The control on line 15 lists it.
Default policy decides allow (read-only-exec) for `tail -f /dev/null & ` x1000 + `tail -f /dev/null`.

blockers: Not observed on the live image: an agent-only sequence that ends with a misleading or absent gui_changes record while a real GUI-made change exists. l9 shows only the first half (agent exec pressure, then agent GUI input, then an empty-baseline burst with no audit marker). The pressure did not release (exit 254, pids stayed at 1022/1024, even after the parent's pkill). The change step and close therefore ran under full pids, and the close logged nothing. Decisive missing facts: (a) whether the agent can release its own pressure through the allowlist, or the cgroup can be left with enough headroom for the open to fail while later steps still work; (b) whether a GUI-made change that needs no new process (for example a shell builtin in a terminal opened before the pressure) is recorded or silently missed at close. The parent must observe this live; this verifier has no Docker access.

No agent-reachable trigger is identified for the exception path at service.py:210/221/238 (a Docker API error, a container not running, or the docker client's 60 s read timeout during collection). This path stays mock-only.

validation_plan.local: Parent-live, Docker-backed, disposable desktop sandbox, dummy human/agent tokens, scratch AGENTBOX_HOME, loopback only. Delete the sandbox afterwards. Variant A (release by agent): (1) As the agent, create 300 files under /workspace (write_file or allowlisted touch), then wait > gui_snapshot_idle. (2) In a background thread, as the agent, call exec with `tail -f /dev/null & ` x~1000 + `tail -f /dev/null`. Expect policy allow / read-only-exec. Poll the container's pids.current from the host until it is >= pids.max - 2. (3) As the agent, POST tools/key {keys: 'shift'}. Record the status, whether box._gui_burst[sid] exists, the manifest size, and the new audit events (l9 already gives: 200, burst with 0 entries, no marker). (4) Release the pressure by an agent-reachable means only (an allowlisted exec such as `pkill -x tail` if it fits in the 1-2 free pids), or kill the tails from the HOST via the cgroup's cgroup.procs (not docker exec, which failed in l9) and record which one was needed. (5) Create /workspace/zz_changed_by_gui.txt with agent GUI tools only (key/type into an Xfce terminal), wait > gui_snapshot_idle, then GET /audit as the human. Expected if the finding holds: the burst has 0 manifest entries, no audit event mentions the collection failure, and gui_changes shows added about 301, truncated=True, with zz_changed_by_gui.txt absent from the listed paths. The control without step 2 must show added=1 with the file listed. Variant B (persistent pressure): open a terminal with GUI tools first, apply the pressure, make the GUI change with a shell builtin (`echo x > /workspace/zz.txt`), and let the burst close under pressure. Record whether the change took effect and whether any gui_changes or error event exists. Refuted for this agent path if the exec cannot fill the cgroup, the snapshot or GUI input fails with 503, or the manifest is complete. Fix check: workspace_manifest/desktop_processes/kill_processes raise SandboxError on a nonzero exit, and _open_gui_burst/_stop_gui_strays/_close_gui_burst log a gui_burst_error audit event and mark the burst baseline invalid, or require human approval for further GUI input until a burst opens with a good baseline. Rerun and expect a gui_burst_error event and no silent empty baseline.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a non-production desktop sandbox: run the same sequence with the deployment's AGENTBOX_DESKTOP_PIDS, AGENTBOX_EXEC_TIMEOUT and AGENTBOX_GUI_SNAPSHOT_IDLE values. Confirm whether the human-facing timeline (web UI audit fragment / CLI) shows any sign that the burst baseline was lost or the collection failed, whether the pressure persists after the agent exec returns, and whether the GUI-made change is visible without restoring the burst snapshot.
